name: Irish Green
lede: Irish Green is a strong, saturated yellow-green from the crowd-sourced xkcd color survey, close enough to the familiar colors of Ireland's flag and shamrock that no painting in our archive carries it.

sections.title: A familiar association, a modern survey
sections.body:
This name comes from the xkcd color survey of 2010, a crowd-sourced naming exercise rather than a historical dye or pigment record, and the ISCC-NBS system separately classifies the same hex value as a strong yellowish green, about 4.6 units from that block's reference color [1]. Neither source states a reason for the name beyond the familiar pairing of green with Ireland [1]. In Munsell terms it reads 0.2G 5.2/11.5, highly saturated for a named color in our library [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[true-green]] and [[forest-green]], at 3 and 3.6 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a color within this measure's threshold of Irish Green covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole; a color this saturated and this modern-feeling is simply absent from the historical works we have measured [2]. It is a useful contrast with [[dresden-brown|Dresden Brown]] in this same batch, present in more than one in five paintings: not every named color has a place in painting's history, even an everyday one like this [2].
